packs.title: Art & Water
packs.promise: Follow art, public waterfronts and a rail journey beyond the old city walls.

q.s: Find a visual connection, then test it against the labels.
st: Use valid MAPR collection admission: budget $20 general plus any tax at checkout, or the applicable documented concession; special exhibitions cost extra and are unnecessary. Galleries open Wednesday, Friday and Saturday 10:00–17:00, Thursday 10:00–20:00 and Sunday 11:00–17:00; Monday, Tuesday and holidays closed. Check the current calendar. Allow 15–25 min admission in addition to this task. Ask which collection rooms are open, leave large backpacks, bundles and non-folding umbrellas at the ticket office and follow note-taking rules.
Choose two displayed works with a shared shape, material or compositional idea. Record each title or other identifying label and one visible detail.
Read both labels. Separate what the labels actually state from your own first interpretation.
Write a two-sentence connection and explain one way the labels supported or changed it.

q.s: Turn an observed public sculpture’s movement into a small composition.
st: Use the open outdoor Juan Morel Campos Plaza in daylight; no performance ticket or theater entry is needed. Respect event fencing and keep the entrances clear. From an open path, choose one bronze Musa that you can see safely and observe without touching.
Make three drawn or written lines describing its pose: a line of balance, a line of movement and a line of space around it.
Change one line to make the movement more pronounced or more still. This is your response, not a tracing or claim about the artist’s intention.
Keep the first and revised versions and give the change a short explanation.

q.s: Compose a view from the city edge toward the sea.
st: Choose an open dry public path at La Ventana al Mar with a view toward the Atlantic. No hotel entry or purchase is required. Stay clear of events and pedestrians, behind barriers and off the beach, breakwater, rocks and wet edges; no water entry is required.
Make a drawing or three short written lines: one for a close public-space edge, one for the middle-ground lawn or path and one for the distant sea.
Give each layer a different visual or verbal weight. Revise one layer so the eye moves more clearly from city to sea.
Record your three layers, revision and a sentence describing the resulting view.

packs.title: Within the Walls
packs.promise: Explore the bay gate, civic streets and northern fort in two connected Old San Juan afternoons.

q.s: Collect three shapes without collecting an object.
st: Use the ordinary open public promenade outside the Raíces fountain basin. No ticket or purchase is needed for this exterior task. Stay on dry paving; water jets and access to every side are not guaranteed.

Find three different visible sculptural forms: one raised above another, one curved, and one that points toward open space. Describe only what you can actually see; a particular figure need not be identified.
Note where each form sits relative to the basin. Finish by choosing the silhouette that is easiest to recognize from a second safe public position; do not enter the basin or step over a barrier.

q.s: Find repetition on the square’s working edge.
st: Use only an open public perimeter pavement with a safe view toward City Hall. This task does not require entering the central plaza, reaching its fountain, sitting on a bench, entering government buildings or passing construction barriers. Follow current work signs; if no safe perimeter view is available, return after access is restored.

Find three visible building details on the City Hall side of the square: a repeated opening, a horizontal division and a shape above the roofline. Describe positions rather than assuming the age or material of each part.
Compare two repeated openings. Write one similarity and one difference that you can actually see from public ground; no complete count or access behind the façade is required.

q.s: Make a new pattern from a tall public artwork.
st: Use open public paving in Plaza del Quinto Centenario, outside the column’s base, steps and any fountain or event enclosure. No climbing, touching, rubbing, entering water or copying carved figures is required. If an event prevents the ordinary view, return in another open window.
Look at El Tótem Telúrico from a safe distance. Note a repeated band and one change in texture or shape without guessing the meaning of a carved motif.

Create your own vertical pattern of three different bands on personal paper or your phone, or describe the pattern in words. Use the observed repetition as a starting point while inventing different marks.
Write which visible feature prompted your pattern and how your three bands differ.
